messages:
Aisha (CS): Heads up — Glyph Solutions just hit a spike in failed responses and slower streams after their latest rollout. Renewal flagged as at-risk; they asked for an ops checklist we can hand to their engineers. Can we draft a short customer-facing runbook focusing on caching, batching, and streaming mitigations?
Devon (Eng-SRE): Yep. Quick priorities: 1) short-term: tenant-scoped hot-prefix cache + 20s TTL, soft refresh on activity. 2) medium: enable small client-side bundling to reduce request overhead. 3) long-term: streaming chunk-size tuning to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Sam (Product): +1. Keep it simple for the customer doc — actionable steps and one SDK snippet per platform. Also include rollback/fallback notes for when we hit capacity.
Marta (Onboarding): Can we add a checklist for their front-end team to mark requests as "priming" vs normal? A header like X-Glyph-Priming=true would help us route into warm pools.
Devon (Eng-SRE): Good call. Suggest we surface these config knobs: 
```json
{"cache_scope":"tenant","cache_ttl_sec":20,"bundle_max_requests":6,"bundle_max_delay_ms":30,"stream_chunk_tokens":64}
```
These are conservative defaults we know are stable on our Dedicated infra.
Aisha (CS): Nice. For the customer-facing one-pager, keep each step two lines max and include the expected impact (e.g., "cache prefix -> cut tail latency by ~40% for repeated prompts").
Sam (Product): Also add a short telemetry checklist: 1) enable request tagging, 2) log per-route p50/p95/p99, 3) capture warm pool hit rate. This will tie to renewal health metrics.
Marta (Onboarding): I'll draft an email-friendly one-pager and a short checklist they can paste into their internal runbook. Want to include a tiny JS SDK snippet for bundling — something like: 
```js
// pseudo
client.batchSend({maxBatch:6, maxWaitMs:30})
```
Keep it minimal.
onboard-bot: Reminder: created draft doc "glyph-cs-runbook-draft-1" in /shared/cs-assets.
Devon (Eng-SRE): Two operational cautions: 1) Watch for cache-miss storms on deployment cutover — add a token bucket limiter on origin fetches. 2) If enabling streaming chunk tuning, keep an emergency toggle to fall back to non-streaming short responses.
Aisha (CS): Action items: @Marta prepare customer doc (due EOD), @Devon add the safe defaults and a short troubleshooting section (error modes + recommended fixes), @Sam add telemetry items and renewal signal mapping. I'll coordinate a 20-min sync with Glyph engineers tomorrow.
Sam (Product): I'll map telemetry -> renewal dashboard hooks. Recommend adding a "quality check" prompt set so they can baseline output similarity after changes.
Marta (Onboarding): Ack. I'll include a short feedback capture template for customer calls: 3 quick questions + a link to the survey.
Devon (Eng-SRE): Quick troubleshooting snippets to include: 
- If tail latency jumps: check warm-pool hit rate, then increase cache_ttl to 30s or bump bundle_max_requests to 8.
- If error rate on fetch: throttle origin with the token bucket and enable async prefill for hot keys.
Aisha (CS): Perfect. Keep the tone customer-friendly, not too prescriptive. We want them to feel empowered, not overwhelmed. :thumbsup:
Sam (Product): Agree. I'll review doc for clarity after Marta's draft.
Marta (Onboarding): Draft uploaded to /shared/cs-assets/glyph-cs-runbook-draft-1.md — ping me for edits.
Aisha (CS): Thanks team. I'll drop this into the renewal playbook and invite Glyph to the sync.
Devon (Eng-SRE): One last thing — include a short snippet for their ops to toggle a fallback model variant if capacity drops. Example header: X-Model-Fallback: small-accel.
Marta (Onboarding): Noted. Sending the invite now. :calendar:
Aisha (CS): Closing thread — will post the final runbook here once revised.
note: This thread is a short operational coordination chat drafted as a single Slack thread string in line with agents.md formatting rules.
